nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_000
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What issues arise due to the inconsistencies between different databases used in LCA?
nodes.answer: Inconsistencies between databases can create problems of comparability between the different analyses performed.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_001
nodes.question: How is NEMO valuable for ecological impact modelling in the transport sector?
nodes.answer: NEMO is valuable for ecological impact modelling in the transport sector as it is used for the mandatory annual compilation of the official Austrian air pollutant and greenhouse gas inventory, allowing for the assessment of transport emissions resulting from different measures and ambition levels up to 2050.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_002
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How has the LBA method been used in various fields, according to M. Sharma et al. (2023)?
nodes.answer: The LBA method has been applied in sustainable practices, transportation, operations, and other areas to assess criteria based on their levels of importance and expert preferences.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What specific type of analysis was implemented to explore the impact of biogenic carbon in the study?
nodes.answer: A dynamic life cycle impact assessment (LCIA) was performed to analyze both short- and long-term emissions including the impact of biogenic carbon.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_004
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What limitation is noted regarding the work of Schulte et al. (2021)?
nodes.answer: Schulte et al. (2021) is limited to a point-value result based on a single scenario for transportation, end-of-life, and material properties.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_005
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How does the lack of complete and quality data impact the LCA methodology?
nodes.answer: The lack of complete and quality data impacts the LCA methodology by affecting the Life Cycle Inventory phase, leading to potential inaccuracies and increased variability and uncertainty in the assessment results.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_006
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: Have any databases been created to address the challenges of the LCA methodology?
nodes.answer: Yes, several databases have been created to address these challenges, but they are often incomplete and outdated.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What life cycle stages were included in the system boundary for the prospective sustainability LCA focusing on impacts to workers?
nodes.answer: The life cycle stages included in the system boundary were transportation and production. This involved cut and sew manufacturing of the leggings and truck drivers transporting the fabric from the textile manufacturing plant to the cut and sew factory and U.S. regional retail distribution centre.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What is the significance of the LBA method proposed by Civic and Paducah (2019) in sustainable practices?
nodes.answer: The LBA method groups criteria according to their levels of significance and allows experts to specify the relevance of the grouped criteria, making it useful in sustainable practices, transportation, operations, etc.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_009
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How does the end-of-life phase of cotton textiles affect the environment?
nodes.answer: In the end-of-life phase, 1.25 kg of cotton textiles are transported 250 km by lorry, contributing to carbon emissions and transportation-related environmental impacts.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_010
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What is the main gap identified in the distribution phase of the Circular Policy Canvas in the outer core of the life cycle?
nodes.answer: The main gap identified in the distribution phase is the lack of policies addressing freight and transportation emissions in the FTI sector, which accounts for a significant share of associated emissions.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Energy for sustainable transportation|Life-cycle analysis of transportation systems_qna_011
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What has become the de facto gold standard for quantifying environmental footprints of agri-food commodity supply chains?
nodes.answer: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) has become the de facto gold standard for quantifying environmental footprints of agri-food commodity supply chains.
